player.//: Movement (src/sim/player/player.ts). A sprint's force-velocity profile: propulsion accel (m/s^2) from a standstill, falling linearly to zero at the top speed for the direction run relative to where the player looks (the ball): maxSpeed forward, sideSpeed sideways (crossover steps, head turned), backSpeed backpedalling. brake: hardest deceleration; grip: all horizontal acceleration (braking, turning, pushing) together, the shoe on sand-filled turf (mu about 0.9). Match data (Miralles et al. 2025, 83 WPT men, WIMU Pro GNSS + LPS): top speed in a match median 15.2 km/h (4.2 m/s), peak acceleration 4.6 and deceleration -4.5 m/s^2 (tracker-smoothed), about 395 accelerations an hour, 80% of them over 1-2 m. Those tracker peaks are sub-maximal (smoothed, and players rarely go flat out); the body can do more: 5 m forward takes 1.56 s here from a standstill (the force build-up of //split included) and 1.45 s once moving; no padel sprint time has been checked yet (OPEN_QUESTIONS.md). The AI uses full effort only when the time left asks for it. sideSpeed, backSpeed and grip are estimates (no published padel figures).
player.//split: Split-step and getting going (FEEL.md, DECISIONS.md Phase 2). Players hop as the opponent strikes: take-off about at their contact, landing 152 ms after it, airborne about 142 ms (world-class tennis, Mecheri et al. 2019); in the air there is no grip. From a static stance force takes time to build: push starts at startFrom of full and reaches it over startRamp; a split-step landing pre-loads the legs (for splitPreload after landing, tuning), so the first step needs no build-up. Calibrated so the split-step reaches a target 1-2.5 m away about 110 ms (11-16% at 1-2.5 m) sooner, as measured (Uzu et al. 2009: 764 vs 868 ms; Nieminen et al. 2014: 13.1%), and with a 170 ms decision the push starts 175 ms after the opponent's contact and the feet have moved 5 cm by 283 ms (tennis, first foot movement: 266-311 ms). splitStepTime is the whole move for the avatar (hop and landing).
player.//reach: Where a ground stroke is met relative to the body's centre: contactFront in front of it (Sanchez-Alcaraz et al. 2021, contact point from the centre of gravity, highly trained players: drive 0.64 +- 0.32 m, lob 0.65 +- 0.32, serve 0.52, volley 0.38, smash 0.45, bandeja -0.01; the game met drives level with the body, 0.00 on average) and reachComfort away from it across the floor (so about 0.67 m out to the side: a drive's contact with the arm nearly straight, the racket's centre about 1 m from the shoulder). Volleys are met VOLLEY_FRONT (0.35 m, positioning.ts) in front and volleyReach away (about 0.6 m out: Sanchez-Alcaraz 0.38 m in front; tennis volleys 0.45-0.70 m out by width, docs/research/serve-and-strokes-motion.md 4.2); overheads overheadReach.

timing.//: Half-widths of the grade windows in seconds; scaled by the timing-window setting.
